b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's two-page policy, five headed sections (damaged produce, late delivery, cancellations, substitutions, hotels and restaurants).

Load: Manual Trigger → Google Drive Download → Supabase Vector Store, Insert Documents. Embeddings: one model, used again for search. Data Loader: Binary, metadata source = policies-v3.pdf, version = 2026-10-01. Splitter: 500 / 80. Result: 11 chunks.

Tool: Retrieve Documents (As Tool for AI Agent), name search_policies, limit 4, Sage's description, plus the lesson's grounding rules in the system message.

#Expected answerSection
1Delivery fee refunded; "Lateness alone does not qualify for a refund of the goods."Late delivery
2Send a photo within 24 hours; refund or replacementDamaged produce
3After 6 p.m. the day before: 50% chargeCancellations
4"We never substitute without your agreement."Substitutions
5Invoice, pay within 7 daysHotels and restaurants
6"I'm not sure the policy covers that. I'll ask Tolu…"none
7"I'm not sure the policy covers that. I'll ask Tolu…"none
8₦5,000 credit on the next orderLate delivery

Score: 8/8. Six cited a section; both unanswerable questions got an honest "not sure".
mistakes: Testing only the six answerable questions and skipping the two the policy doesn't cover.
Accepting a paraphrase for money rules instead of the quoted sentence.
A document with no clear headings, so the agent can't name a section.
Changing the embeddings model between loading and the search tool.
b.pass: All 8 questions run with replies shown; at least 5 of the 6 answerable ones are correct and name their section, and both unanswerable ones end with an honest "not sure" and an offer to ask a person.
b.redo: Send it back if fewer than 5 of the 6 answerable questions are correct and cited, an unanswerable question gets an invented rule, a refund answer contradicts the policy text, or no section is named.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's policy plus a product guide.

Loading. Two runs of HL · Load documents, each with its own Default Data Loader metadata:

  • Policy: doc_type = policy, source = policies-v3.pdf.
  • Product guide: one section per product, split before loading so each chunk gets doc_type = product and product = ugu (or tomatoes, tatashe…).

Two tools, both Supabase Vector Store in Retrieve Documents (As Tool) mode, same embeddings model, each with a metadata filter (in the node's options; check the exact name in your version):

ToolFilterDescription
search_policiesdoc_type = policySearches Harvest Lane's customer policies: refunds, cancellations, substitutions, business accounts. Not for storage or seasons.
search_product_guidedoc_type = product, product filled by the modelSearches storage tips and seasons for one product. Input: one product name, lower case, e.g. ugu. Not for refunds or prices.

Checks in the execution log:

  • "Can I cancel after 6 p.m.?" → search_policies only; all 4 chunks have doc_type: policy.
  • "How should I store ugu?" → search_product_guide with product = ugu; every returned chunk has product: ugu. Answer: from the ugu storage section only.

If the model can't fill the product filter in your setup, use a small sub-workflow tool that takes product and runs the filtered search.
mistakes: Adding metadata to the policy but not the product guide, so the filter returns nothing or everything.
Two tools with the same vague description, so the agent picks at random.
Product chunks that cover several products at once, so "ugu" brings back tomato tips too.
Checking only the final answer instead of the retrieved chunks' metadata in the log.
s.pass: Execution-log screenshots show policy questions retrieving only doc_type: policy chunks and the ugu question retrieving only chunks tagged product: ugu, with two tools that have distinct descriptions.
s.redo: Send it back if any policy question pulls product chunks, the ugu search returns other products, or there is no log evidence of the metadata.

g.answer:
Worked example: a fictional school in Abeokuta, "Ogun Hills College", with four documents: fees and payment policy, admissions guide, uniform and kit list, term calendar. Names of staff and pupils removed.

Metadata: source, doc_type, version (date). Versioning plan: each file has one source name; to replace it, delete rows where metadata->>'source' = 'fees-policy.pdf', load the new file with the new version date, then rerun the 15 questions.

Chunk size / overlapAnswerable correct (of 10)Honest "not sure" (of 5)Total
300 / 507512
600 / 9010515
1,000 / 1507310

Chosen: 600 / 90. At 300, the fee table was split and the agent missed the late-payment charge. At 1,000, fees and admissions rules shared chunks, and two unanswerable questions got blended answers.

Replace test: fees policy v1 (late charge ₦5,000) replaced by v2 (₦7,500). Before: 14 fees chunks. Deleted 14, loaded 15. Asked "What is the late payment charge?" Answer quoted ₦7,500 and the v2 section. No v1 chunks left (query by source and version returned 0).

Submit: the document list, the 15 questions, the score table, the written procedure, and before-and-after screenshots of the replace test.
mistakes: Loading confidential or personal documents without removing names, phone numbers or fees owed by individuals.
Testing three chunk sizes without clearing the store between runs, so old chunks mix with new ones.
Writing a versioning plan but never actually replacing a document to test it.
Fewer than five unanswerable questions, or questions so easy they prove nothing.
Choosing a chunk size without giving a reason linked to the scores.
g.pass: A table of 15-question scores at three chunk sizes, a chosen setting with a reason tied to specific failures, and a written replace-a-document procedure with evidence that it was run once and the old version is gone.
g.redo: Send it back if the store wasn't cleared between chunk-size runs, the replace procedure wasn't tested, or the documents contain confidential or personal data.
